explanation: Anticoagulants cause bleeding including hemopericardium. Multiple published case reports (PMID:22786838, 26798391, 29259514). Well-known class risk despite being absent from the specific labeled AE list; not a novel finding.
Not a pharmacologic AE. FDA Class I recalls of BD ChloraPrep for microbial/fungal contamination 2020-2025 drove the reporting volume.
Same as 'Product contamination physical' at the MedDRA HLT level; double-counted.
Macrolide ototoxicity is labeled since 1994. Reversible or irreversible sensorineural hearing loss documented across macrolides (PMID:10778901). Systematic review in Sci Rep 2023.
The MedDRA PT 'Labelled drug-disease interaction medication error' is itself a medication-error term, not a drug-caused adverse event.

Alkindi is hydrocortisone replacement therapy FOR primary adrenal insufficiency in pediatric patients. Reports reflect missed or inadequate dosing in the treated disease — the 'event' IS the indication.
Monistat-1 (tioconazole) PI lists vulvar edema and vulvovaginal irritation at <1-6% incidence. Labeled local reaction of vaginal antifungal.
Tamoxifen retinopathy/maculopathy with crystalline deposits is classic and in the ocular-effects section of the current label. Review PMID:37482306.
Extrinsic brown tooth staining is the universally labeled side effect of chlorhexidine mouthrinse (Peridex PI) and documented in countless clinical trials.
Class IC sodium-channel blockade mechanistically prolongs the QRS. This is the labeled dose-titration endpoint (reduce dose if QRS widens >25%), not an adverse signal.
Blincyto (blinatumomab) is indicated for relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor ALL. The 'event' IS the treated disease relapsing — disease-progression reports, not drug causation.
Historical FDA-documented Teva Budeprion XL 300 mg bioequivalence problem (2012). MedDRA 'Product substitution issue' is itself a medication-error term.
Regadenoson is a rapid IV push for pharmacologic stress testing. Extravasation is a generic peripheral-IV administration complication, not a regadenoson pharmacology signal.
Device-hygiene complaint. Linked to Perrigo albuterol HFA clogging recalls; a reporting/device artifact, not pharmacology.
Urocit-K is a wax-matrix extended-release tablet; 'ghost tablet' excretion in stool is expected and documented in the PI. Not a safety signal.
Jesduvroq (daprodustat) is FDA-approved solely for anemia of chronic kidney disease (= nephrogenic anemia). The event IS the treated condition.
Depo-Testosterone is a supersaturated oil solution; crystallization or deposit at low storage temperature is a documented expected product behavior (Pfizer PI).
BSS Plus is a cataract-surgery irrigating solution. Endophthalmitis is a post-operative surgical complication of the procedure, not a drug-caused AE.
2024-2025 Class II recalls of levothyroxine products (Mylan, Lupin, Accord/Intas) for potency issues. Narrow-therapeutic-index drug + switching guidance drives reporting.
Monistat PI explicitly lists 'temporary increase in burning, itching, or irritation' as the most common AE (~2-7% in trials) of vaginal miconazole.
Etelcalcetide is for secondary hyperparathyroidism in dialysis patients. Arteriovenous shunt issues are dialysis-access procedural confounders, not a drug effect.
Same as shunt occlusion — dialysis-access context in the treated population, not etelcalcetide pharmacology.
Topical lidocaine is used routinely during foreign-body removal procedures. The PT reflects the procedural context, not a drug effect.
Lidocaine is used during bronchoscopy and airway FB removal — the event names the procedure context.
Fibrin formation in the anterior chamber is a cataract-surgery complication, not an effect of the irrigation fluid itself.
Intravitreal Lucentis (ranibizumab) injection site effect — procedural complication of repeated injections, not a pharmacologic signal.
Injection-site bleb after intravitreal ranibizumab — procedural/local.
Gadolinium IS a contrast media by definition. The MedDRA PT 'Contrast media reaction' naming the drug class is a meta-artifact.
Not causation — reports of hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients receiving ondansetron in oncology settings. Known interaction risk rather than a novel signal.
Pediatric oral-administration context — reflux/spitting-up in infants receiving sprinkle formulations is an administration issue, not steroid pharmacology.
Documented in anesthesia literature (several case reports) but not widely in labels. Worth deeper PubMed review before classifying.
Potentially novel — sulfonylurea + biliary malignancy association is not labeled. Needs literature search and population context.
